findings.reason: the plan's premise is stale and its fix is one call-site resolution plus one guard, so a worker sent to "move the stopping line" in dispatch.py broadly would edit the wrong seam.
findings.text: §2 asserts every read-only resolution "is simply not reached when `dry_run` is set", but the dry-run branch already calls `plan_dispatch` (reckon/cli.py:2052) and that function already resolves the plan section and its review (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5529-5543) whenever `repo is not None`; the real remaining gap is only that the dry-run call site passes the raw `--repo` while the real path resolves the project mount first (`repo_root = resolve_project_repository(project, repo)`, dispatch.py:6586), and that the section gate is skipped when `repo is None` (dispatch.py:5486)

findings.reason: a second parity harness will drift from the first; the plan should extend the existing comparison file rather than add parallel ones.
findings.text: §2 and §3 each propose a new test file (test_dry_run_resolves_the_real_call.py, test_member_resolution_is_single_valued.py) for assertions that already exist: tests/test_dispatch_result_matches_launch.py:561 asserts every dry-run refusal carries error/detail, :385 asserts an unresolvable member is refused with nothing bound, and tests/test_dry_run_reaches_admission.py and tests/test_dry_run_predicts_the_launcher.py:159 already hold admission and launcher/refusal parity

findings.reason: the honest change is a stop point on `dispatch()`, the module that owns the sequence, not a parallel dry branch that must be kept in step.
findings.text: §2's "move the line the dry run stops at" is realised by adding resolution work to the cli.py dry branch, a thin forwarder that re-emits each refusal, and the plan never says why the real path cannot be extended instead, although `shadow()` already demonstrates the pattern it needs (a `dry_run` argument that calls `plan_dispatch` and returns before dispatch, reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6097)

findings.reason: §2's done-when asserts the two payloads "equal", which institutionalises the duplicate; `dispatch()` owns the refusal semantics and should be extended with the stop point rather than mirrored.
findings.text: the dry-run block emits twelve separate refusal documents (`_with_resolved_overrides`, cli.py:2077-2255) carrying the same `error` keys and exit codes the live-path handlers derive from `dispatch()`'s exceptions (cli.py:2280-2464: budget-hold 3, plan-unavailable/plan-review-missing 4, competence-refusal 5, watcher-required 8, tmp-headroom 75), so the mapping has two owners

findings.reason: the mechanism cannot meet its own done-when; the dry run must execute `dispatch()`'s resolution sequence up to the worktree boundary, not `plan_dispatch` alone.
findings.text: §2's done-when requires the dry run to "refuse what the real call refuses", but its mechanism is `plan_dispatch`, which never raises the dispatch()-internal precondition refusals: the unreconciled-run refusal is raised in `dispatch()` after `plan_dispatch` returns and before any worktree exists (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6724-6746), so a dry run extended only at `plan_dispatch` still answers `ok` for a dispatch that would exit 6

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design edits the existing resolver rather than introducing a new module, so it adds no shallow module; the surface it does add is a parallel path in cli.py, which duplicate_owner names, not a new module.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the dry-run branch in reckon/cli.py re-implements the refusal-to-exit-code mapping owned by `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:dispatch()` (6511), and `plan_dispatch` alone cannot reach the dispatch()-internal refusals the done-when demands.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan proposes making the dry run "reach" resolutions it says are skipped, but the dry-run branch already calls the shared resolver `plan_dispatch` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5192) and already runs the plan/section visibility gate (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5529); the plan cites neither, so both its premise and its fix target are misplaced.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2 keeps the cli.py dry-run branch as a thin parallel resolution path that forwards to `plan_dispatch` while re-listing every refusal, without saying why the real path's own function cannot gain a stop-before-worktree mode.
